US: Average of state rates; pick your state for a closer estimate
AL: 2% state auto rate plus local; local rates vary widely
AK: No state sales tax; a few boroughs charge a local tax
AR: 6.5% state plus local; doc fee capped at $129
CA: 7.25% state plus local (LA and Bay Area run 9.5%-10.25%); doc fee capped at $85
CO: 2.9% state plus local; Denver metro runs 8%-9%
DE: No sales tax; the DMV charges a 4.25% document fee instead
DC: Excise tax of 6%-8% set by weight and mpg; most EVs are exempt
FL: 6% state plus a county surtax (up to 1.5%) on the first $5,000; doc fees are among the highest
GA: One-time 7% Title Ad Valorem Tax replaces sales tax
HI: 4% excise tax plus county surcharge (4.712% on Oahu)
IL: 6.25% state plus local (Chicago about 10.25%); doc fee capped near $358
IA: 5% one-time registration fee instead of sales tax; doc fee capped at $180
LA: 5% state plus local (often 9%-10.5%); doc fee capped at $425
MD: 6.5% titling tax (raised from 6% in July 2025); doc fee capped at $500
MN: 6.875% motor vehicle sales tax; doc fee capped at $125
NJ: 6.625%; an extra 0.4% applies to some vehicles over $45,000
NY: 4% state plus local (NYC 8.875%); doc fee capped at $175
NC: 3% highway use tax instead of sales tax
OH: 5.75% state plus county; doc fee capped at $250
OR: No sales tax; a 0.5% vehicle privilege tax is usually passed on to the buyer
TN: 7% state plus local tax on the first $1,600
TX: 6.25% statewide; no local tax on vehicles
VA: 4.15% sales and use tax; doc fees are among the highest
WA: 6.5% state plus 0.3% motor vehicle tax plus local (Seattle about 10.5%); doc fee capped at $200
